findings: legacyImportSender.ts (bulk CSV import path) sends only {orderId, amount} and omits the `currency` field entirely, directly violating the v2 payload contract documented as 'currency added in v2, always present per the docs' -- the contract and the code disagree for this one send path.

consumer.ts calls `payload.currency.toUpperCase()` with no null/undefined guard, so any payload missing `currency` throws a TypeError at `.toUpperCase()` and crashes the handler; since the partner coded strictly against the 'always present' doc guarantee, they had no reason to defend against it, but the guarantee is false for import-sourced orders.

legacyImportSender.ts is explicitly noted as 'written before v2 existed' and was never updated when the v2 currency field was introduced -- webhookSender.ts (checkout) was migrated to the v2 shape but its legacy counterpart was not, so the codebase silently has two senders emitting two different (v1 vs v2) payload shapes at the same documented v2 endpoint with no payload version field or content-based way for the consumer to discriminate which shape it received.

This exactly reproduces the reported symptom: crashes occur only for bulk CSV import orders (via legacyImportSender, missing currency) and never for normal checkout orders (via webhookSender, which includes currency), confirming the root cause is the unmigrated legacy sender rather than any consumer-side defect.

There is no default/fallback for currency in legacyImportSender.ts (e.g. defaulting to a base currency) and no schema validation at the webhook send boundary, so an incomplete v1-shaped payload is sent to partners under the v2 contract unchecked, rather than being caught, upgraded, or explicitly versioned before transmission.
